references.text: The curtain that the pillars were to support is described in the preceding verse, which forms the immediate context for the pillars and their construction.
The pillars of the courtyard gate also had bronze bases and gold hooks, showing similar construction methods in the tabernacle.
This verse describes the actual fulfillment of the command in Exodus 26:37, with five acacia wood pillars, gold-plated hooks, and bronze bases.
Acacia wood (שִׁטִּים) is mentioned here as one of the materials to be gathered for the construction of the tabernacle.
The four pillars of the inner curtain had a similar construction with acacia wood and gold plating, but with silver bases instead of bronze.
The courtyard pillars also had bronze bases and silver hooks, illustrating the hierarchical system of materials in the tabernacle.

The description of the execution of the curtain's pillars is compared with the original instructions, highlighting the contrast in material (silver vs. bronze) as a textual-critical or theological point regarding its fulfillment.
